$comment: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for how this pipeline carries values.
Every wall this codebase hit was one mistake said twice: an exact integer
carried in a float. Slot ordinals aliased past 2^24. Pick ID bases alias past
2^24. foldScalars lane 0 (totalRows) aliases past 2^24. Each layer decided,
independently and in a comment, what kind each field was, and the copies drifted.
KIND is the declared fact. CONTAINER is a per-layer realization of it.
count / identity / bitfield   exact. MUST NOT ride a float carrier — and a
float ordered key IS a float carrier wearing a
u32 costume, which is how totalRows hid.
measure                       a real quantity. f32 is correct and its
rounding is load-bearing.
Layers may realize kinds differently and stay conformant — the engine uses four phase arrays (see buffers.$comment), the render side one homogeneous atomic buffer where kind is per-lane. It used two
buffers (where a value lives IS its kind, so it cannot be got wrong), while the
TSL side uses one homogeneous atomic buffer where kind is per-lane. Neither is
privileged. What each layer owes is that its generator ASSERT its own mapping
respects the kinds, so both realizations are checkable rather than trusted.
The engine's per-array strides are DERIVED from kind below and asserted
against it, so its container cannot disagree with the declaration.
SEVEN ARRAYS, SPLIT TWICE — and, since 2026-08-31, ZERO declared deviations.
First split, WRITE axis — who WRITES a lane decides where it lives:
static      decode's output: a pure function of the byte through the trie.
Written once per byte as one aligned 16-byte store; never
rewritten (FLAGS is the exception: the fold ORs in F_RENDERED).
positional  the fold's output: requires sequential state. Decode NEVER
touches it — that is the entire point. Zeroing of non-leader
bytes belongs to the fold (which walks every byte of its item
anyway) and to a driver sweep over the known GAP ranges.
Second split, READ axis — who READS a lane decides whether it lives at all:
witness     fold interior state (LINE_ADV, ORD) that no render path reads.
The scan form allocates it (its resolve step consumes it); the
serial form writes it only in the WITNESS instantiation, which
is what the suites run. Production runs elided and a cross-check
pins the two instantiations' render-read arrays bit-identical.
Measured before building the first split: 1.37x end-to-end on decode+fold
(engine/bench/split_bench.mojo), because the cost of dispatch 1 is DIRTIED
CACHE LINES, not stores. The read-axis split continues the same ledger: the
elided fold dirties 28 B per byte (lm 16 as ONE aligned SIMD store + lc 8 +
flags 4) where the witnessed fold dirties 44 and pays an ord_to_byte memset
besides (engine/bench/elide_bench.mojo).
THE RECORD IS UNCHANGED — both times. The wire order [X Y Z ADVANCE HEIGHT
GLYPH_ID][ROW COL] still partitions at the phase boundary: posMeasures'
render-read prefix (0-2), staticMeasures' (0-2), then posCounts WHOLE — the
read-axis split made the record's count section and the container coincide.
The generator pins the wire as a literal; a restructure that moves it fails
the build.
GLYPH_ID is a native u32 identity (staticIdentities) as of the trie format
moving to u32 (50fd6b8). SM_PAD died with it: the pad existed to align a
16-byte static store that no longer needs four lanes. staticMeasures is two
genuine measures and nothing else; the wire BYTES did not move (GLYPH_ID
still sits at record offset 20 — only its run classification changed, from
the measure run's tail to the count run's head).

lanes.name: FLAGS
lanes.note: Read with bitwise ops by later dispatches, so not render-scratch.

lanes.name: Y
lanes.note: Addressed POSITIONALLY as X+1 in glyphVertex.js — a search for S_Y misses that read.

lanes.name: Z
lanes.note: Addressed POSITIONALLY as X+2 in glyphVertex.js.

lanes.name: LINE_ADV
lanes.note: The fold's f64 line prefix, narrowed once per leader. Read by the scan form's foldless x and by the suites; the serial form writes it only under the witness instantiation.

lanes.name: ORD
lanes.note: The lane that started all of this. Aliased past 2^24 as an f32; exact to 2^32 as a native count. Witness tier since the read-axis split: the render path never reads it, so the serial form writes it only when witnessed.

lanes.name: GLYPH_ID
lanes.note: The system's oldest deviation, settled 2026-08-31. It rode the f32 staticMeasures array for as long as the trie handed decode an f32 — the misplaced entry named its own fix ('cannot move until the TRIE FORMAT moves'), the trie moved (50fd6b8), and the stale-declaration rule made keeping the exemption a build failure. Exact to 2^32 now, end to end.

identities.name: slotOrdinal
identities.note: Per-ITEM, not per-arena: ord resets for each item.

identities.name: pickId
identities.witness: a readback for a known glyph must resolve to that glyph
identities.broken: Rides a FLOAT uniform today (uniform(0) from a JS number). Aliases past 2^24; the guard admits 0x7FFFFFFF, 127x too permissive, and WARNS rather than refuses. Reachable since the arena passed 2^24.

$comment: The segmented monoid's element (ScanElem), as it lives in a GPU buffer.
Same rule as the slot buffers: counts and measures are different arrays.
tail_adv is the ONLY measure — it is an f32 sum accumulated per-add, which
is what makes the reduce exact under regrouping. Everything else is a count.

lanes.name: RESET
lanes.note: absorbing: combine(a,b)=b when b.reset — file isolation is structural

lanes.name: WRAP
lanes.note: a QUERY parameter carried in the element, not file state

lanes.name: TAIL_ADV
lanes.note: f32 per add — the discipline that makes the reduce exact under regrouping

$comment: THIS BACKEND'S per-item layout table, on device — split by carrier like every
other table in the system (2026-08-31, the kind correction): world-unit
distances in f32, integer page geometry native u32. It was one f32 array of
15 lanes until the render side's carrier split made a question askable that a
mixed container cannot pose — does each param ride the carrier its KIND
requires? — and five counts failed it. They were declared 'measure' because
this table's section was literally NAMED measures: the container had defined
the kind, the exact inversion the tier split exists to prevent. The paginate
kernel's own war story (119 glyphs on the wrong page from a ULP wobble in a
float page key) is the ground truth of what kind these values are.
Every lane still declares realizes/realization_only/orphan against the
semantic set; the carrier rule now runs over THIS table too (the miss
survived precisely because it did not).

lanes.name: PAGE_STRIDE_X
lanes.derived: PAGE_GAP_X + the item's widest row (bounds lane MAX_ROW_EXTENT). This layer derives on the host and stores the result; the render side stores the gap and derives on device. Both realize the same semantic parameter.

lanes.name: HAS_PAGE
lanes.realization_only: encodes ABSENCE of a page. The render side encodes the same fact as a null page object with zeroed geometry.

$comment: Per-item bounds + fold scalars. 8 lanes, and lane 6 is why this section exists.
TOTAL_ROWS is a COUNT (row + 1) that the TSL side stores via floatToOrderedKey —
an exact integer on a float carrier, aliasing past 2^24. Reachable: S_ROW is the
VISUAL row, so at wrap=1 rows track glyph count, crossing 2^24 at ~16.8MB inside
a 44.7MB arena. foldGeometry.js:146 has been doing Math.trunc(p.totalRows || 0) —
a consumer defensively truncating a count back to an integer, which is a
downstream compensating for an upstream that lost its type.
The engine's CPU form holds all 8 in f64, which is exact to 2^53 and has no wall,
so there is no defect there. On DEVICE it must split: Metal has no f64, and an
f32 ordered key would alias exactly as the TSL side does. The hardware forces the
same answer the kind rule already required.

carrier f64 = the HOST realization (device uses u32 ordered keys + native u32 counts). Declared 2026-08-31: a section with no carrier is unvalidatable by construction — every carrier rule silently skips it, which is how TOTAL_ROWS rode f64 undeclared while its f32 cousins were being hunted.

lanes.name: TOTAL_ROWS
lanes.note: the fold scalar the TSL side carries as a float ordered key — see above
lanes.misplaced: A count on the host's f64 bounds array. Unlike the f32 walls, this is provably lossless — rows are bounded by byte count (u32) and 2^32 < 2^53 — and the DEVICE realization is already a native u32 atomicMax (BOUNDS_COUNT_LANES exists for exactly this lane). Declared so the carrier rule can SEE it rather than skip an undeclarable section; settle by splitting the host bounds container by carrier, the same dance as every other table.

lanes.name: MAX_ROW_EXTENT
lanes.note: item-relative widest fold row; genuinely a measure, keeps the ordered key

$comment: The per-item layout parameters, as SEMANTICS. This is the set both layers
must be able to express; it is NOT anyone's item table.
It exists because the first version of ITEM_PARAMS was emitted from the
engine's itemTable with the strides removed — the same container leak the
tier split fixed, one level subtler: the strides went and the SHAPE stayed.
Asserted against, it produced five failures of which ONE was a real gap and
four were 'we made different, equally valid container choices'. A check that
reports four false positives per true one trains its reader to ignore it.
PAGE_GAP_X is named by the INPUT, not by the derived stride. A caller supplies
a gap; the fan stride is (widest item-relative row + gap) and WHERE that
derivation happens is each layer's business — the render side derives it on
device from a fold scalar, the engine derives it on the host. Same fact.
Deliberately NOT here, as realization rather than semantics:
HAS_PAGE     one layer carries an explicit flag, the other encodes absence
as a null page with zeroed geometry. Two encodings of 'no page'.
BYTE_COUNT   the item's extent, not a layout parameter. One layer keeps it
in the item table because its kernels resolve ownership on
device; the other resolves it elsewhere.
PAGE_STRIDE_X as distinct from the gap — a derivation point, see above.

params.name: WRAP_WIDTH
params.note: the fold unit; overrides PAGE_COLS when nonzero

params.name: LINE_HEIGHT
params.note: world y per row. REQUIRED — never the glyph's own height

params.name: SCROLL_ROWS
params.note: Integer page geometry — consumed through truncation at every read site in every layer, which was the seam confessing the kind all along. Corrected measure->count 2026-08-31.

params.name: PAGE_ROWS
params.note: Integer page geometry — consumed through truncation at every read site in every layer, which was the seam confessing the kind all along. Corrected measure->count 2026-08-31.

params.name: PAGE_COLS
params.note: also the fold unit when WRAP_WIDTH is 0

params.name: PAGES_WIDE
params.note: Integer page geometry — consumed through truncation at every read site in every layer, which was the seam confessing the kind all along. Corrected measure->count 2026-08-31.

params.name: PAGE_GAP_X
params.note: world x gap between fanned page columns — the INPUT; the stride is derived from it plus the widest item-relative row
